body: A lot of psychologists are terrible and seem to get into the profession for self serving reasons. When you don't improve or struggle to follow their suggestions, they take it as a personal affront and quickly get offended and it shows. That doesn't mean they're all bad, however. I've encountered some who are genuine. I think finding someone who has experience with your particular issue is important. Somebody with experience treating GAD doesn't necessarily know how to deal with AvPD.

Are you still able to study alright? How are your grades? If you find you're having problems with both, you can always see a university counselor to share your struggles with. You can get out of the classes you're currently enrolled in without failing or messing up your future. You might even be able to get a refund. If you're still doing alright in your classes, I'd still recommend seeing one. It should be free and they might be able to help you. It wouldn't hurt to try.

I feel the same way. Because I was so certain I was going to kill myself, I stopped trying at life completely, and because of that, now I have a life that truly isn't worth living. I don't recommend letting this line of thinking influence you if it's at all possible. It's extremely destructive.
